title: Close a roll-top bread bin: draw its slatted tambour along the curved grooves, over the corner and down the front
context: Roll-top bread bins, desks and cabinets close with a tambour: a row of slats whose pins run in curved grooves, so the handle has to be drawn along the grooves' path, forward round the rounded corner and down, and any pull across that path binds the pins. Closing one is an everyday kitchen chore.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. (1) A bamboo roll-top bread bin fixed to the counter, front toward the robot: side panels 393 mm apart outside (344 mm inside) from x 185 to 480, 185 mm tall, rounded over the front corner, a bottom board, a back and a top board from x 275 back. A loaf (160 x 180 x 80 mm) is inside. (2) In each side panel's inner face, a 9 mm groove 10 mm deep: up the front at x 205 from 25 mm, round the corner on a 50 mm radius about x 255, z 115, and back along the top at 165 mm to x 465. (3) The tambour, 0.33 kg: thirteen bamboo slats, each 16 mm wide, 8 mm thick and 340 mm long with a 6 mm pin at each end in the grooves, joined edge to edge so that each joint can fold up to 26 degrees one way. The front slat carries a 120 mm handle ridge standing 12 mm proud. It starts open: flat along the top run, the handle slat's pins at x 263, the handle standing up just in front of the top board.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial. 1.0 (success, must hold for 1 s) when the bin is shut: the handle slat's pins within 4 mm of the grooves' lower ends at the bottom of the front run, both grippers 30 mm or more from the handle slat and nothing moving more than 1 mm for 1 s; 0.75 when it is shut but a gripper is near or the tambour still moves; 0.5 when the handle slat has been drawn past the curve onto the front run but is not shut; 0.25 when the handle slat was moved 30 mm along the grooves at some point; else 0.
reset_notes: Push the tambour back up the front, round the corner and along the top until the handle slat is just in front of the top board.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size. The tambour is thirteen rigid slats on a chain of hinges, each joint folding one way only (as the cloth backing of a real tambour allows); their pins slide in grooves cut in exact mesh side panels, with wood-on-wood friction. The bin is fixed. All geometry is generated by code in the package.
